what: The registration of the demo layer's optional online overlay. 06_build_layer.py writes 60_layer/overlay.js from it; without this file the layer has no overlay and says so.
year_parameters: start_year and end_year are added by the page from the window chosen for the decision view
documented_at: https://tiles.globalforestwatch.org/openapi.json - the specification behind the provider's own reference pages https://tiles.globalforestwatch.org/ and https://tiles.globalforestwatch.org/docs. It states the path /umd_tree_cover_loss/{version}/dynamic/{z}/{x}/{y}.png, the versions (latest, v1.11, v1.12, v1.13) and the query parameters start_year, end_year, render_type and tree_cover_density_threshold. It names no host: by the OpenAPI rule the host is the one that serves the document
documentation_is: a machine-generated API reference on the tile host. There is no prose guide; the provider's developer help does not name the tile host
version_is_pinned: v1.13 is in the address. The alias 'latest' is not used: it moves to the next release without notice
canopy_setting: tree_cover_density_threshold=10: loss on land with about 10 % tree canopy or more in 2000, the dense and the open band of the decision view together. The reference says 'greater than or equal to this threshold'; the unit tables use strictly above 10
max_native_zoom_is: this layer's own setting, not a limit of the provider: a tile at zoom 12 is already at the data's full resolution, and the layer enlarges it beyond that. The provider's reference allows zoom up to 22
tiles_are: 512-pixel PNG on the ordinary web-map grid; with render_type=true_color, pink on transparent. Below zoom 12 a tile is an aggregate shaded by the density of loss
attribution: Source: Hansen/UMD/Google/USGS/NASA. Global Forest Change v1.13, CC BY 4.0. Tiles served by Global Forest Watch (World Resources Institute)
data_licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), stated in the provider's dataset record https://data-api.globalforestwatch.org/dataset/umd_tree_cover_loss and on the University of Maryland's page for v1.13
terms_cover: The address https://www.globalforestwatch.org/terms/ redirects to this page, 'Terms of Service | Global Nature Watch'. It names resourcewatch.org, globalforestwatch.org and prepdata.org among the sites it covers, 'owned and operated by the World Resources Institute'. The tile host's own reference is titled 'GFW Tile Cache API'
terms_say: Use of the services is agreement to the terms. 'You may not use the Services in any manner that could damage or overburden the Services or interfere with any other party's use of the Services.' 'If You use Our APIs in Your own products, please credit Us. You agree to attribute our APIs in line with our Attribution Requirements, available at [https://resourcewatch.org/api-attribution-requirements].' 'We may cancel or suspend Your access to the Services at any time and for any reason, without notice.' No rate limit is published; the words tile, embed and hot-link do not occur
attribution_requirements_page: https://resourcewatch.org/api-attribution-requirements - it speaks of 'the Resource Watch API': 'Websites that use the Resource Watch API must include the "powered by Resource Watch" logo linking to http://resourcewatch.org on pages that make use of the Resource Watch API.' and 'Graphics, charts, and maps created using the Resource Watch API must include the text and link "powered by Resource Watch" if the Resource Watch logo does not appear elsewhere on the page'. The same page says: 'This site is no longer being updated and will be archived in the coming months.' The overlay's attribution carries no such words
terms_unresolved: Two points, both the project owner's to decide; one note to gfw@wri.org could settle both. (1) API keys. The terms read 'each request to an API must include one of Your Account's unique API keys'. The tile service's reference declares no key scheme and the service returns every tile without one. The provider's developer page counts the Tile Cache among the Data API's five core services and says 'Some endpoints require users to include an API key with their request'; the guide it links says 'To make most requests to the GFW Data API using third-party applications (e.g., scripts or websites), you need an API key.' Nothing read says whether tiles drawn in a page like this one are among them. (2) Attribution. The terms bind a user to the Attribution Requirements page, which asks for the words and link 'powered by Resource Watch' on maps made with 'the Resource Watch API'. Whether that page governs the tile service of Global Forest Watch is not said anywhere read, and the page is to be archived. The overlay credits the data's authors, its licence and the tile provider, and does not carry those words
verified_how: Two independent searches and an adversarial verifier read the provider's reference, dataset record and terms on 8 Oct 2026; tiles over central Odisha were fetched at zoom 9 and 12 (HTTP 200, image/png) with canopy settings 10 and 30 and with and without a year range, and decoded: the year range and the canopy setting each change the pixels shown, as the reference says. On the same day an adversarial review read the terms, the attribution page, the developer pages, the dataset record and the tile reference again and corrected this record; every sentence quoted here was then found in a copy of each page fetched at the time given above
what_is_sent: only requests for tiles, to the registered host and no other, and only while the box is ticked: each carries the tile's place and zoom and the years of the window chosen, with the browser's usual headers. Opened from disk, the page has no web address of its own to pass on
provider_cautions: From the provider's record of the dataset (https://data-api.globalforestwatch.org/dataset/umd_tree_cover_loss), in its words: 'Tree cover loss is defined as "stand replacement disturbance" which is considered to be clearing of at least half of tree cover within a 30-meter pixel. The exact threshold is variable both through space and time, and is biome-dependent.' 'In this data set, "tree cover" is defined as all vegetation greater than 5 meters in height, and may take the form of natural forests or plantations across a range of canopy densities.' '"loss" does not equate to deforestation.' 'current (post-2000) tree cover cannot be determined by subtracting figures for annual tree cover loss from year 2000 tree cover.' 'The 2011-2025 data was produced using an updated methodology ... Comparisons between the original 2001-2010 data and the 2011-2025 update should be performed with caution.' 'the authors are 75% confident that the loss occurred within the stated year, and 97% confident that it occurred within a year before or after.' The original publication put false positives at 13% and false negatives at 12% overall
provider_cautions_are: Global Forest Watch's record of the dataset, not a statement of the University of Maryland, from whose data (through Earth Engine) the unit tables are built
pages_kept: five of the pages read on 8 Oct 2026 - the dataset record, the terms, the attribution page, the tile service's reference and the University of Maryland's page for v1.13 - are registered in 00_raw/05_forest_reference/ since 9 Oct 2026, each with a manifest row; the provider's developer page and its guide to API keys, which the note on the unresolved terms also quotes, are still only with the session's working files (.session_scratch_2026-10-05/overlay_pages_2026-10-08/)
provider_cautions_now_live_in: 00_raw/05_forest_reference/provider_cautions.json, from which the layer's About text quotes them whether or not the overlay is shipped; the key provider_cautions here is kept as it was
